git merge vs git rebase — when do you use each?

Merge joins histories with a merge commit and never rewrites anything, so it is safe on shared branches. Rebase replays your commits on top of another branch for a linear history; use it on your own feature branch before opening a PR (git pull --rebase, git rebase -i to squash). 💡 Golden rule: never rebase commits that others have already pulled.
git reset vs git revert?

reset moves the branch pointer back (soft keeps changes staged, mixed keeps them unstaged, hard discards them) and rewrites history — fine locally. revert adds a new commit that undoes an earlier one, so it is the safe way to undo something already pushed to a shared branch.
You committed a password and pushed it. What do you run?

First rotate the secret — assume it is compromised. Then remove it from history with git filter-repo --path secrets.env --invert-paths (or BFG), force-push, and ask everyone to re-clone. Add the file to .gitignore and a pre-commit secret scanner so it cannot happen again.
npm install vs npm ci?

npm install may update package-lock.json within allowed ranges. npm ci deletes node_modules and installs exactly what the lock file says, failing if it is out of sync — reproducible and faster, so it is what CI pipelines (Jenkins) should use.
A Spring Boot service is using 100% CPU in production. Which commands do you run?

top -H -p <pid> to find the hot thread id, convert it to hex (printf '%x' <tid>), then jstack <pid> and search for that nid to see the stack. Take 2–3 thread dumps a few seconds apart; also check GC with jstat -gcutil <pid> 1000 — constant full GCs look like CPU load too.
How do you debug a container that keeps restarting?

docker ps -a for the exit code (137 = killed, often OOM; 1 = app error), docker logs --tail 200 <c> for the stack trace, and docker inspect <c> for env vars, mounts and OOMKilled. In Kubernetes: kubectl describe pod (events) and kubectl logs --previous.
Port 8080 is already in use. How do you find and stop the process?
Linux/macOS: lsof -i :8080 or ss -tulpn | grep 8080, then kill -15 <pid> (and -9 only if it will not stop). Windows: netstat -ano | findstr :8080, then taskkill /PID <pid> /F.
kill -15 vs kill -9?

SIGTERM (15) asks the process to shut down — Spring Boot runs its graceful shutdown, finishes in-flight requests and closes connection pools. SIGKILL (9) cannot be caught; the JVM dies immediately with no cleanup. Always try 15 first; Docker stop sends SIGTERM then SIGKILL after the timeout.
How do you find which dependency pulls in a conflicting library version?
Maven: mvn dependency:tree -Dincludes=group:artifact; Gradle: ./gradlew dependencyInsight --dependency artifact. Then pin the version in dependencyManagement / a platform BOM or add an exclusion.
docker compose down vs docker compose down -v?
Both stop and remove containers and networks; -v also deletes named volumes — i.e. your database data. Use plain down (or restart) unless you deliberately want a clean database.
How do you see the last 100 errors in a log file and count them by type?
grep "ERROR" app.log | tail -n 100 for the latest ones, and grep -o "[A-Za-z.]*Exception" app.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr to count exceptions by type. Add -C 5 to grep to see surrounding lines.
How do you upgrade an Angular project to the next major version?

Upgrade one major at a time: ng update @angular/core@18 @angular/cli@18 (then third-party libs like Material), commit, run tests, and repeat. The command runs migration schematics that rewrite code automatically; check the Angular update guide for manual steps.
